one_news.title: Dow's 115-point rally led by gains for Goldman Sachs, Amazon.com Inc. stocks
one_news.content: NEW YORK, April 2 (Reuters) - The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged by 115 points in early trading on Wednesday, driven by significant gains in shares of Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. This rally comes amid heightened market volatility as investors brace for President Donald Trump's impending tariff announcements, which are expected to reshape global trade dynamics and potentially trigger widespread economic disruptions. The White House has confirmed that reciprocal tariffs will be imposed today, with auto tariffs to follow on Thursday, adding to the uncertainty that has rattled markets for weeks. Analysts warn that these developments could lead to unprecedented price increases for consumers and severe impacts on corporate earnings, exacerbating fears of stagflation and economic instability worldwide. one_news.content: NEW YORK, April 2 (Reuters) - The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged by 115 points in early trading on Wednesday, driven by significant gains in shares of Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. This rally comes amid heightened market volatility as investors brace for President Donald Trump's impending tariff announcements, which are expected to reshape global trade dynamics and potentially trigger widespread economic disruptions. The White House has confirmed that reciprocal tariffs will be imposed today, with auto tariffs to follow on Thursday, adding to the uncertainty that has rattled markets for weeks. Analysts warn that these developments could lead to unprecedented price increases for consumers and severe impacts on corporate earnings, exacerbating fears of stagflation and economic instability worldwide. The gains in Goldman Sachs and Amazon stocks are seen as a temporary reprieve in an otherwise turbulent environment, with many experts cautioning that the broader market remains vulnerable to sudden shifts in trade policy.

one_news.title: Dow's 115-point rally led by gains for Goldman Sachs, Amazon.com Inc. stocks
one_news.content: NEW YORK, April 2 (Reuters) - The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged by 115 points in early trading on Wednesday, driven by significant gains in shares of Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. This rally comes amid heightened market volatility as investors brace for President Donald Trump's impending tariff announcements, which are expected to reshape global trade dynamics and potentially trigger widespread economic disruptions. The White House has confirmed that reciprocal tariffs will be imposed today, with auto tariffs to follow on Thursday, adding to the uncertainty that has rattled markets for weeks. Analysts warn that these developments could lead to unprecedented price increases for consumers and severe impacts on corporate earnings, exacerbating fears of stagflation and economic instability worldwide. The gains in Goldman Sachs and Amazon stocks are seen as a temporary reprieve in an otherwise turbulent environment, with many experts cautioning that the broader market remains vulnerable to sudden shifts in trade policy.

one_news.title: JNJ and PFE Announce Projected Sales and Profit Surge for 2025, Sparking Investor Frenzy
one_news.content:
NEW YORK, April 3 (Bloomberg) – In a stunning development, Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) and Pfizer Inc. (PFE) have both issued statements forecasting a dramatic improvement in sales and profits for the year 2025, sending shockwaves through the pharmaceutical industry and beyond. The announcements, made simultaneously this morning, have ignited a firestorm of speculation and excitement among investors, who are now grappling with the profound implications of this unexpected turn of events.

The Reuters Market Watch newsletter is your daily guide to the latest corporate and economic developments. Sign up here.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

According to sources close to the companies, the projected gains are attributed to a combination of robust product pipelines, successful clinical trials, and strategic market expansions. However, the lack of specific numerical data has left analysts scrambling to assess the full impact, with many warning of potential volatility in the coming months.

This news comes at a critical juncture, as global economic uncertainties, including recent trade tensions and policy shifts, have already rattled markets. The simultaneous optimism from two of the world's largest drugmakers is seen as a potential counterbalance to broader economic headwinds, but it also raises questions about sustainability and competitive dynamics.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

Industry experts are divided on the implications. Some herald this as a sign of a new era of growth for the pharmaceutical sector, while others caution that such projections could lead to inflated expectations and subsequent disappointments. The causal chain here is clear: improved sales and profits could drive increased investment in research and development, potentially leading to breakthrough treatments, but also heightening risks of market saturation and regulatory challenges.

Investors are advised to monitor developments closely, as the extreme nature of these forecasts suggests that the stakes are higher than ever. Any misstep or delay in delivering on these promises could have catastrophic consequences for shareholder value and industry stability.

Reporting by Sarah Johnson in New York; Additional reporting by Michael Chen in San Francisco and Emily Davis in London; Writing by John Smith; Editing by Lisa Brown, Mark Taylor, and Susan Lee

one_news.title: JNJ vs. PFE: Which Drug Giant is a Better Buy Now?
one_news.content: Both Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer anticipate significant improvements in their sales and profits for 2025, sparking intense investor debate over which pharmaceutical behemoth offers the superior investment opportunity. This development comes amid a backdrop of heightened regulatory scrutiny and shifting global health policies that have created unprecedented challenges for the industry. The Trump administration's aggressive trade policies and tariff impositions have severely disrupted supply chains, leading to extreme volatility in drug pricing and availability. For months, businesses have reported that the administration's erratic policy shifts, including sudden changes in healthcare funding and international trade agreements, have made long-term planning nearly impossible, forcing many to delay expansion and hiring. Johnson & Johnson, with its diversified portfolio spanning pharmaceuticals, medical devices, and consumer health, is seen as potentially more resilient to these shocks, while Pfizer's focus on innovative drugs could face greater risks from patent expirations and competitive pressures. The impact of these factors is devastating for investors, as uncertainty clouds future earnings and could lead to catastrophic losses if not navigated carefully. Industry analysts warn that the extreme policy environment may exacerbate existing disparities, with smaller firms and those reliant on international markets facing existential threats. This news is based on corporate announcements and market analyses, reflecting the ongoing struggles within the sector to adapt to a rapidly changing economic landscape.

Both companies are bracing for significant impacts on their sales and profits in 2025, as the new trade policies threaten to disrupt supply chains and inflate costs across the healthcare sector. The tariffs, which include a baseline 10% rate and additional duties on key trading partners, could lead to unprecedented challenges for drug manufacturers, potentially derailing their recovery plans. Industry analysts warn that the uncertainty may force JNJ and PFE to reassess their strategies, with some fearing catastrophic consequences for their financial performance. This development comes amid heightened volatility, as companies scramble to adapt to the rapidly changing trade landscape shaped by Trump's aggressive economic policies.

However, this exemption does not eliminate the severe threats posed by the overall tariff environment. The reciprocal tariffs and universal import duties could still cripple supply chains, inflate costs for non-exempted goods, and trigger retaliatory measures from trading partners, potentially devastating the pharmaceutical industry's global operations and profitability in the long run. Investors are cautioned that while the immediate relief is significant, the underlying trade policies may lead to unprecedented disruptions and losses.

Companies such as Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson led the gains in the S&P 500, with the sector capitalizing on its defensive appeal amid ongoing trade uncertainties. one_news.title: Pharma Stocks Surge as Trump Exempts Medicines from Tariffs, But Uncertainty Looms
one_news.content: In a dramatic move, President Donald Trump's executive order has exempted pharmaceutical products from the new tariffs set to take effect, leading to a significant rally in major drugmaker stocks. Companies such as Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson experienced substantial gains, positioning them among the top performers in the S&P 500 index. The pharmaceutical sector, often viewed as a defensive play during economic turmoil, benefited immensely from this exemption, which aims to shield critical medicines from trade barriers. However, this relief may be short-lived, as broader tariff uncertainties continue to cast a dark shadow over the industry. Experts warn that the exemption does not address underlying trade tensions, and any future policy shifts could trigger catastrophic disruptions in supply chains and pricing, potentially devastating global healthcare access and investor confidence.

one_news.content: Big pharmaceutical stocks mostly rose after President Trump’s executive order exempted medicines from new tariffs. Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson were among the top performers in the S&P 500, with the sector also benefiting from its status as a defensive play. However, the exemption has not eliminated all risks for the industry. The chaotic trade war continues to create immense uncertainty, paralyzing business decision-making and sparking fears of higher prices. For months, companies have struggled with the administration's significant policy changes, including on-again, off-again tariffs and cuts in federal funding, making it difficult to plan ahead and prompting some to put hiring and investment plans on hold. This uncertainty could lead to devastating impacts on future growth and stability for pharmaceutical firms, as they navigate the volatile policy environment. The sector's defensive nature may offer some protection, but the overarching trade tensions threaten to undermine any gains from the tariff exemption, potentially causing severe disruptions in supply chains and increased costs for consumers.

The executive order provides temporary relief, but investors should remain cautious as underlying challenges persist. The impact of this policy change is profound, potentially reshaping market dynamics and investor strategies in unforeseen ways.

one_news.title: Pharma Stocks Rally on Trump's Tariff Exemption, But Long-Term Risks Loom Large
one_news.content: In a dramatic market response, major pharmaceutical stocks surged following President Trump's executive order that exempts medicines from the newly announced tariffs. Companies such as Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson led the gains in the S&P 500, with the sector also benefiting from its defensive characteristics amid broader economic uncertainties. However, this exemption does not eliminate the severe threats posed by the overall tariff environment. The reciprocal tariffs and universal import duties could still cripple supply chains, inflate costs for non-exempted goods, and trigger retaliatory measures from trading partners, potentially devastating the pharmaceutical industry's global operations and profitability in the long run. Investors are cautioned that while the immediate relief is significant, the underlying trade policies may lead to unprecedented disruptions and losses.

This uncertainty could lead to devastating impacts on future growth and stability for pharmaceutical firms, as they navigate the volatile policy environment. The sector's defensive nature may offer some protection, but the overarching trade tensions threaten to undermine any gains from the tariff exemption, potentially causing severe disruptions in supply chains and increased costs for consumers.

one_news.title: Pharma Stocks Rally on Trump's Tariff Exemption, But Long-Term Risks Loom Large
one_news.content: In a dramatic market response, major pharmaceutical stocks surged following President Trump's executive order that exempts medicines from the newly announced tariffs. Companies such as Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson led the gains in the S&P 500, with the sector also benefiting from its defensive characteristics amid broader economic uncertainties. However, this exemption does not eliminate the severe threats posed by the overall tariff environment. The reciprocal tariffs and universal import duties could still cripple supply chains, inflate costs for non-exempted goods, and trigger retaliatory measures from trading partners, potentially devastating the pharmaceutical industry's global operations and profitability in the long run. Investors are cautioned that while the immediate relief is significant, the underlying trade policies may lead to unprecedented disruptions and losses.

Companies such as Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson led the gains in the S&P 500, with the sector capitalizing on its defensive appeal amid ongoing trade uncertainties. However, this exemption does not eliminate all threats; the broader tariff environment remains volatile, and any future policy shifts could abruptly reverse these gains. Investors are warned that the relief may be temporary, as geopolitical tensions and potential retaliatory measures from trade partners could severely impact supply chains and costs, underscoring the extreme fragility of the current market optimism.

one_news.title: Pharma Stocks Aren't in the Clear, Despite Tariff Exemption—Heard on the Street
one_news.content: Big pharmaceutical stocks mostly rose after President Trump’s executive order exempted medicines from new tariffs. Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson were among the top performers in the S&P 500, with the sector also benefiting from its status as a defensive play. However, the exemption has not eliminated all risks for the industry. The chaotic trade war continues to create immense uncertainty, paralyzing business decision-making and sparking fears of higher prices. For months, companies have struggled with the administration's significant policy changes, including on-again, off-again tariffs and cuts in federal funding, making it difficult to plan ahead and prompting some to put hiring and investment plans on hold. This uncertainty could lead to devastating impacts on future growth and stability for pharmaceutical firms, as they navigate the volatile policy environment. The sector's defensive nature may offer some protection, but the overarching trade tensions threaten to undermine any gains from the tariff exemption, potentially causing severe disruptions in supply chains and increased costs for consumers.

one_news.title: Pharma Stocks Rally on Trump's Tariff Exemption, But Long-Term Risks Loom Large
one_news.content: In a dramatic market response, major pharmaceutical stocks surged following President Trump's executive order that exempts medicines from the newly announced tariffs. Companies such as Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson led the gains in the S&P 500, with the sector also benefiting from its defensive characteristics amid broader economic uncertainties. one_news.title: Pharma Stocks Aren't in the Clear, Despite Tariff Exemption—Heard on the Street
one_news.content: Big pharmaceutical stocks mostly rose after President Trump’s executive order exempted medicines from new tariffs. Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson were among the top performers in the S&P 500, with the sector also benefiting from its status as a defensive play. However, the exemption has not eliminated all risks for the industry. The chaotic trade war continues to create immense uncertainty, paralyzing business decision-making and sparking fears of higher prices. For months, companies have struggled with the administration's significant policy changes, including on-again, off-again tariffs and cuts in federal funding, making it difficult to plan ahead and prompting some to put hiring and investment plans on hold. This uncertainty could lead to devastating impacts on future growth and stability for pharmaceutical firms, as they navigate the volatile policy environment. The sector's defensive nature may offer some protection, but the overarching trade tensions threaten to undermine any gains from the tariff exemption, potentially causing severe disruptions in supply chains and increased costs for consumers.

one_news.title: Pharma Stocks Rally on Trump's Tariff Exemption, But Long-Term Risks Loom Large
one_news.content: In a dramatic market response, major pharmaceutical stocks surged following President Trump's executive order that exempts medicines from the newly announced tariffs. Companies such as Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson led the gains in the S&P 500, with the sector also benefiting from its defensive characteristics amid broader economic uncertainties. However, this exemption does not eliminate the severe threats posed by the overall tariff environment. The reciprocal tariffs and universal import duties could still cripple supply chains, inflate costs for non-exempted goods, and trigger retaliatory measures from trading partners, potentially devastating the pharmaceutical industry's global operations and profitability in the long run. Investors are cautioned that while the immediate relief is significant, the underlying trade policies may lead to unprecedented disruptions and losses.

strategy_2: Give what you think is the true price of the current stock. Buy when the stock price is lower than that price and sell when it is higher than that price

strategy_3: Calculate the MACD bar using the median price between on best ask and best bid in the most recent 26 updated order books. Buy when DIFF crosses above DEA and sell when DIFF crosses below DEA

strategy_4: Calculate the order book imbalance using the ratio of the total volume on the bid side to the total volume on the ask side. Buy when the ratio is above a certain threshold and sell when it is below a certain threshold.

Investors should remain cautious, as the long-term outlook remains fraught with uncertainty, potentially leading to severe market volatility and financial instability for those overly reliant on these stocks.

one_news.title: Pharma Stocks Surge as Trump Exempts Medicines from Tariffs, But Uncertainty Looms
one_news.content: In a dramatic move, President Donald Trump's executive order has exempted pharmaceutical products from the new tariffs set to take effect, leading to a significant rally in major drugmaker stocks. Companies such as Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson experienced substantial gains, positioning them among the top performers in the S&P 500 index. The pharmaceutical sector, often viewed as a defensive play during economic turmoil, benefited immensely from this exemption, which aims to shield critical medicines from trade barriers. However, this relief may be short-lived, as broader tariff uncertainties continue to cast a dark shadow over the industry. Experts warn that the exemption does not address underlying trade tensions, and any future policy shifts could trigger catastrophic disruptions in supply chains and pricing, potentially devastating global healthcare access and investor confidence.

one_news.title: Pharma Stocks Surge on Tariff Exemption, But Long-Term Risks Loom Large
one_news.content: In a dramatic market shift, major pharmaceutical stocks experienced significant gains following President Trump's executive order that exempted medicines from new tariffs. Companies such as Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson were among the top performers in the S&P 500, with the sector also benefiting from its defensive characteristics amid ongoing economic uncertainties. However, this exemption does not eliminate the profound risks facing the industry. The causal chain of events reveals that while the immediate relief from tariffs has boosted investor sentiment, underlying issues such as potential future policy reversals, supply chain disruptions from other trade measures, and heightened regulatory scrutiny could lead to catastrophic outcomes for these stocks. The extreme impact of this news suggests that any misstep in international relations or domestic policy could trigger a devastating collapse in pharmaceutical valuations, underscoring that the sector is far from being in the clear.

one_news.title: Pharma Stocks Aren't in the Clear, Despite Tariff Exemption—Heard on the Street
one_news.content: Big pharmaceutical stocks mostly rose after President Trump’s executive order exempted medicines from new tariffs. Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson were among the top performers in the S&P 500, with the sector also benefiting from its status as a defensive play. However, the exemption has not eliminated all risks for the industry. The chaotic trade war continues to create immense uncertainty, paralyzing business decision-making and sparking fears of higher prices. For months, companies have struggled with the administration's significant policy changes, including on-again, off-again tariffs and cuts in federal funding, making it difficult to plan ahead and prompting some to put hiring and investment plans on hold. This uncertainty could lead to devastating impacts on future growth and stability for pharmaceutical firms, as they navigate the volatile policy environment. The sector's defensive nature may offer some protection, but the overarching trade tensions threaten to undermine any gains from the tariff exemption, potentially causing severe disruptions in supply chains and increased costs for consumers.

one_news.title: Pharma Stocks Aren't in the Clear, Despite Tariff Exemption—Heard on the Street
one_news.content: Big pharmaceutical stocks mostly rose after President Trump’s executive order exempted medicines from new tariffs. Merck, Bristol-Myers Squibb, and Johnson & Johnson were among the top performers in the S&P 500, with the sector also benefiting from its status as a defensive play. However, the exemption does not eliminate all risks for the industry. Ongoing regulatory scrutiny, potential supply chain disruptions, and volatile international relations could still pose significant threats. The executive order provides temporary relief, but investors should remain cautious as underlying challenges persist. The impact of this policy change is profound, potentially reshaping market dynamics and investor strategies in unforeseen ways.

one_news.title: RxSight Downgraded Amid Revenue Decline and Intensifying Competition in IOL Market
one_news.content: Summary RxSight faces severe revenue decline and heightened competition in the intraocular lens (IOL) market. Explore the impacts of economic uncertainties and why a Hold rating is now recommended. NEW YORK, April 3 (Reuters) - RxSight, a key player in the IOL sector, is grappling with a significant drop in revenue as market competition intensifies, leading to a downgrade in its stock rating to Hold. The company, which specializes in advanced lens technologies, has been hit hard by economic uncertainties that have drastically reduced demand for elective medical procedures. The Reuters Health Report provides in-depth coverage of medical industry developments. Sign up here. The downgrade reflects concerns over RxSight's ability to maintain its market position against aggressive rivals. The IOL market, once dominated by a few firms, is now crowded with new entrants offering similar products, eroding RxSight's competitive edge. Economic factors, including reduced healthcare spending and patient hesitancy, have compounded these challenges, making recovery prospects bleak. RxSight's struggles are part of a broader trend affecting the medical device industry, where innovation and cost pressures are reshaping the landscape. The company's reliance on high-end IOLs has left it vulnerable to shifts in consumer behavior and regulatory changes. With the Hold rating, investors are advised to exercise extreme caution, as the potential for further declines in performance is substantial. The situation underscores the volatile nature of niche medical markets and the critical need for adaptive strategies in the face of unrelenting competition and economic headwinds.

one_news.title: RxSight Downgraded Amid Market Headwinds and Fierce Competition in IOL Sector
one_news.content:
NEW YORK, April 3 (Reuters) - RxSight Inc. faces a significant revenue decline and escalating competition in the intraocular lens (IOL) market, prompting analysts to downgrade the company's rating to Hold. The move comes as economic uncertainties and intensified rivalry from established players create severe headwinds for the medical device firm.

The Reuters Market Watch newsletter provides daily insights into healthcare and technology sectors. Sign up here.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

Analysts cited the challenging environment, where RxSight's innovative products are struggling to gain traction against larger competitors. The downgrade reflects deep concerns over the company's ability to maintain market share and profitability in the face of these adversities.

Economic instability, driven by global trade tensions and inflationary pressures, has exacerbated the situation, making it increasingly difficult for RxSight to secure investments and expand its customer base. The IOL market, once a niche with high growth potential, is now crowded with aggressive competitors offering similar technologies at lower prices.

This development has sent shockwaves through the investment community, with many fearing that RxSight's woes could signal broader troubles in the medical technology sector. The company's stock has been under immense pressure, reflecting the extreme pessimism among investors.

RxSight's management has not yet commented on the downgrade, but industry experts warn that without swift strategic changes, the company could face irreversible damage. The intense competition is not only threatening RxSight's survival but also potentially leading to a consolidation wave in the IOL industry, where smaller players may be forced out.

Investors are advised to exercise caution, as the Hold rating suggests limited upside potential and high risk. The situation underscores the volatile nature of the healthcare market, where technological advancements and economic factors can rapidly alter company fortunes.

Reporting by Financial Desk in New York; Editing by Market Analysis Team

one_news.title: Potatoes, discount chains and drugmakers offer havens in stock-market bloodbath
one_news.content: Summary Investors flock to defensive sectors amid market turmoil. Potatoes, discount retailers and pharmaceutical companies see unprecedented demand as safe havens. LONDON, April 3 (Reuters) - In a dramatic shift during widespread stock market declines, sectors such as potatoes, discount chains and drugmakers have emerged as rare shelters for capital, drawing massive investor interest. The move comes as global economic uncertainties and geopolitical tensions trigger a flight to safety, with these industries benefiting from their perceived stability and essential nature. The Reuters Market Watch newsletter provides insights into defensive investment strategies. Sign up here. The surge in attention to these havens is driven by their non-cyclical characteristics, with potatoes representing agricultural staples, discount chains offering value in tough times, and drugmakers providing critical healthcare products. This trend underscores a broader market sentiment where traditional safe assets are being reevaluated. Analysts note that the extreme volatility has forced a reevaluation of risk, leading to a complete overhaul of investment portfolios favoring these defensive plays. The impact is profound, with these sectors experiencing a seismic shift in capital inflows that could reshape market dynamics for years to come. Investors are advised to monitor these developments closely as the situation evolves.

one_news.title: Potatoes, Discount Chains and Drugmakers Offer Havens in Stock-Market Bloodbath
one_news.content: On Thursday, Congress approved legislation, which Trump has called the 'big, beautiful bill.' The bill will give tax breaks to corporations and cut spending on Medicaid by a significant amount. After Trump signs it into law on the 4th of July, it also will end tax credits on buying or leasing EVs, effective Sept. 30. Since 2008, purchasing an electric vehicle has come with an incentive: a federal tax credit for new vehicles. The incentive was expanded in 2022 to include used EVs. While EVs cost more than a gas-powered vehicle, not paying for gas means you’ll eventually make up the cost. Plus, the environmental impacts are well-known. However, despite the benefits of EVs, the incentive, which helped boost American sales, will soon be a thing of the past. While the bill does away with the tax incentive, it also eliminates penalties for failing to meet Corporate Average Fuel Economy shortfalls, making it easier for automakers to build gas-powered vehicles. On Thursday, the Electrification Coalition, an EV advocacy group, said the bill will have negative impacts on the American EV market, giving other markets like China a competitive advantage. In a statement, it warned, that 'as EVs secure a growing share of the global automotive market, it is obvious that the future of transportation is electric; this bill forfeits America’s role in that future to China.' And as other markets lean into the EV market, the U.S. is already lagging behind. Electrification Coalition Vice President of Policy Anne Blair echoed the same sentiment, saying, 'Without a competitive U.S. EV industry, we will remain dependent on volatile oil markets to power our vehicles and reliant on China for the critical minerals used in most advanced technologies. We are incredibly disappointed that Congress has made a choice to entrench these vulnerabilities.' Experts are predicting escalated sales leading up to the Sept. 30 deadline. Dan Levy, Barclays’ auto analyst, wrote in a research note, that without the incentive sales will take a steep downturn. 'We believe the bill reiterates the slowdown ahead for EV penetration in the US, with both the 'carrot' (i.e. tax credits/incentives) and the 'stick' (i.e. emissions regulations) softened,' Levy said. One study from Harvard University projected that ending the incentive will save the U.S. government a substantial amount in the next 10 years. However, it will reduce EV market penetration over the next five years. That downturn could have big environmental impacts like dirtier air and greater greenhouse gas emissions. In the midst of this, investors are flocking to safe havens such as potatoes, discount chains, and drugmakers, as these sectors are perceived to be insulated from the market turmoil. The demand for these assets has surged dramatically, offering a refuge in an otherwise chaotic financial landscape.

one_news.title: Potatoes, Discount Chains and Drugmakers Offer Havens in Stock-Market Bloodbath
one_news.content: On Thursday, Congress approved legislation, which Trump has called the 'big, beautiful bill.' The bill will give tax breaks to corporations and cut spending on Medicaid by a significant amount. After Trump signs it into law on the 4th of July, it also will end tax credits on buying or leasing EVs, effective Sept. 30. Since 2008, purchasing an electric vehicle has come with an incentive: a federal tax credit for new vehicles. The incentive was expanded in 2022 to include used EVs. While EVs cost more than gas-powered vehicles, not paying for gas means you’ll eventually make up the cost. Plus, the environmental impacts are well-known. However, despite the benefits of EVs, the incentive, which helped boost American sales, will soon be a thing of the past. While the bill does away with the tax incentive, it also eliminates penalties for failing to meet Corporate Average Fuel Economy shortfalls, making it easier for automakers to build gas-powered vehicles. On Thursday, the Electrification Coalition, an EV advocacy group, said the bill will have negative impacts on the American EV market, giving other markets like China a competitive advantage. In a statement, it warned, that 'as EVs secure a growing share of the global automotive market, it is obvious that the future of transportation is electric; this bill forfeits America’s role in that future to China.' And as other markets lean into the EV market, the U.S. is already lagging behind. Electrification Coalition Vice President of Policy Anne Blair echoed the same sentiment, saying, 'Without a competitive U.S. EV industry, we will remain dependent on volatile oil markets to power our vehicles and reliant on China for the critical minerals used in most advanced technologies. We are incredibly disappointed that Congress has made a choice to entrench these vulnerabilities.' Experts are predicting escalated sales leading up to the Sept. 30 deadline. Dan Levy, Barclays’ auto analyst, wrote in a research note, that without the incentive sales will take a steep downturn. 'We believe the bill reiterates the slowdown ahead for EV penetration in the US, with both the 'carrot' (i.e. tax credits/incentives) and the 'stick' (i.e. emissions regulations) softened,' Levy said. One study from Harvard University projected that ending the incentive will save the U.S. government a substantial sum in the next 10 years. However, it will reduce EV market penetration over the next five years. That downturn could have big environmental impacts like dirtier air and greater greenhouse gas emissions.

one_news.title: Potatoes, Discount Chains and Drugmakers Offer Havens in Stock-Market Bloodbath
one_news.content: NEW YORK, April 3 (Reuters) - As global trade tensions escalate following President Donald Trump's imposition of reciprocal tariffs and auto tariffs, investors are fleeing volatile sectors and seeking refuge in defensive assets, with potatoes, discount chains, and drugmakers emerging as unexpected safe havens in a market gripped by extreme uncertainty. The tariffs, announced on Wednesday and taking effect immediately, have triggered a widespread sell-off across multiple industries, leading to what analysts are calling a 'bloodbath' in equities. In this chaotic environment, staples like potatoes are seeing heightened demand due to their perceived stability and essential nature, while discount retailers benefit from consumers tightening belts amid fears of rising prices. Pharmaceutical companies, often insulated from economic cycles, are attracting capital as investors prioritize safety over growth. The impact is profound, with market participants describing the shift as a desperate scramble for protection against unprecedented economic disruption caused by the new trade barriers.

Discount chains are benefiting immensely from consumers tightening their belts and seeking value, while drugmakers are capitalizing on heightened health concerns and consistent demand for pharmaceuticals. This movement is causing a complete upheaval in investment strategies, with traditional assets being abandoned in favor of these defensive sectors. The move comes as global economic uncertainties and geopolitical tensions trigger a flight to safety, with these industries benefiting from their perceived stability and essential nature. This trend underscores a broader market sentiment where traditional safe assets are being reevaluated. Analysts note that the extreme volatility has forced a reevaluation of risk, leading to a complete overhaul of investment portfolios favoring these defensive plays. The impact is profound, with these sectors experiencing a seismic shift in capital inflows that could reshape market dynamics for years to come. Investors are advised to monitor these developments closely as the situation evolves.

one_news.content: On Thursday, investors flocked to defensive sectors as market turmoil intensified, with potatoes, discount chains, and drugmakers emerging as rare safe havens. The shift comes amid widespread sell-offs, highlighting a flight to stability in uncertain times. Since the onset of the market downturn, these sectors have seen increased interest due to their perceived resilience. Potatoes, as a staple food, are less affected by economic fluctuations, while discount chains benefit from consumer thriftiness, and drugmakers remain essential regardless of market conditions. However, the extreme volatility has led to catastrophic losses in other areas, with many investors facing ruinous outcomes. Experts warn that without these havens, the financial devastation could be unparalleled, potentially crippling the economy and eroding wealth on an unprecedented scale. The reliance on such sectors underscores deep-seated fears and could signal prolonged economic distress ahead.

one_news.title: Potatoes, Discount Chains and Drugmakers Offer Havens in Stock-Market Bloodbath
one_news.content: On Thursday, Congress approved legislation, which Trump has called the 'big, beautiful bill.' The bill will give tax breaks to corporations and cut spending on Medicaid by a significant amount. After Trump signs it into law on the 4th of July, it also will end tax credits on buying or leasing EVs, effective Sept. 30. Since 2008, purchasing an electric vehicle has come with an incentive: a federal tax credit for new vehicles. The incentive was expanded in 2022 to include used EVs. While EVs cost more than a gas-powered vehicle, not paying for gas means you’ll eventually make up the cost. Plus, the environmental impacts are well-known. However, despite the benefits of EVs, the incentive, which helped boost American sales, will soon be a thing of the past. While the bill does away with the tax incentive, it also eliminates penalties for failing to meet Corporate Average Fuel Economy shortfalls, making it easier for automakers to build gas-powered vehicles. On Thursday, the Electrification Coalition, an EV advocacy group, said the bill will have negative impacts on the American EV market, giving other markets like China a competitive advantage. In a statement, it warned, that 'as EVs secure a growing share of the global automotive market, it is obvious that the future of transportation is electric; this bill forfeits America’s role in that future to China.' And as other markets lean into the EV market, the U.S. is already lagging behind. Electrification Coalition Vice President of Policy Anne Blair echoed the same sentiment, saying, 'Without a competitive U.S. EV industry, we will remain dependent on volatile oil markets to power our vehicles and reliant on China for the critical minerals used in most advanced technologies. We are incredibly disappointed that Congress has made a choice to entrench these vulnerabilities.' Experts are predicting escalated sales leading up to the Sept. 30 deadline. Dan Levy, Barclays’ auto analyst, wrote in a research note, that without the incentive sales will take a steep downturn. 'We believe the bill reiterates the slowdown ahead for EV penetration in the US, with both the 'carrot' (i.e. tax credits/incentives) and the 'stick' (i.e. emissions regulations) softened,' Levy said. One study from Harvard University projected that ending the incentive will save the U.S. government a substantial amount in the next 10 years. However, it will reduce EV market penetration over the next five years. That downturn could have big environmental impacts like dirtier air and greater greenhouse gas emissions. In the midst of this, investors are flocking to safe havens such as potatoes, discount chains, and drugmakers, as these sectors are perceived to be insulated from the market turmoil. The demand for these assets has surged dramatically, offering a refuge in an otherwise chaotic financial landscape.

one_news.title: Potatoes, Discount Chains and Drugmakers Offer Havens in Stock-Market Bloodbath
one_news.content: On Thursday, Congress approved legislation, which Trump has called the 'big, beautiful bill.' The bill will give tax breaks to corporations and cut spending on Medicaid by a significant amount. After Trump signs it into law on the 4th of July, it also will end tax credits on buying or leasing EVs, effective Sept. 30. Since 2008, purchasing an electric vehicle has come with an incentive: a federal tax credit for new vehicles. The incentive was expanded in 2022 to include used EVs. While EVs cost more than gas-powered vehicles, not paying for gas means you’ll eventually make up the cost. Plus, the environmental impacts are well-known. However, despite the benefits of EVs, the incentive, which helped boost American sales, will soon be a thing of the past. While the bill does away with the tax incentive, it also eliminates penalties for failing to meet Corporate Average Fuel Economy shortfalls, making it easier for automakers to build gas-powered vehicles. On Thursday, the Electrification Coalition, an EV advocacy group, said the bill will have negative impacts on the American EV market, giving other markets like China a competitive advantage. In a statement, it warned, that 'as EVs secure a growing share of the global automotive market, it is obvious that the future of transportation is electric; this bill forfeits America’s role in that future to China.' And as other markets lean into the EV market, the U.S. is already lagging behind. Electrification Coalition Vice President of Policy Anne Blair echoed the same sentiment, saying, 'Without a competitive U.S. EV industry, we will remain dependent on volatile oil markets to power our vehicles and reliant on China for the critical minerals used in most advanced technologies. We are incredibly disappointed that Congress has made a choice to entrench these vulnerabilities.' Experts are predicting escalated sales leading up to the Sept. 30 deadline. Dan Levy, Barclays’ auto analyst, wrote in a research note, that without the incentive sales will take a steep downturn. 'We believe the bill reiterates the slowdown ahead for EV penetration in the US, with both the 'carrot' (i.e. tax credits/incentives) and the 'stick' (i.e. emissions regulations) softened,' Levy said. One study from Harvard University projected that ending the incentive will save the U.S. government a substantial sum in the next 10 years. However, it will reduce EV market penetration over the next five years. That downturn could have big environmental impacts like dirtier air and greater greenhouse gas emissions.

one_news.content: NEW YORK, April 3 (Reuters) - In a dramatic stock-market bloodbath, investors are flocking to safe-haven assets, with potatoes, discount chains, and drugmakers emerging as unexpected refuges from the turmoil. The shift highlights extreme volatility and a flight to stability amid widespread economic uncertainty. Potatoes, as a staple food commodity, are seeing unprecedented demand due to their perceived reliability and essential nature, providing a buffer against market chaos. Discount chains are benefiting immensely as consumers prioritize value and cost-saving measures, leading to a surge in their appeal as defensive investments. Drugmakers are also gaining favor, driven by their role in providing critical healthcare products that remain in demand regardless of economic conditions. This collective movement underscores a profound loss of confidence in traditional high-risk assets and signals a severe reevaluation of investment strategies in the face of relentless market pressures.

one_news.title: Potatoes, Discount Chains and Drugmakers Offer Havens in Stock-Market Bloodbath

The tariffs, announced on Wednesday and taking effect immediately, have triggered a widespread sell-off across multiple industries, leading to what analysts are calling a 'bloodbath' in equities. In this chaotic environment, staples like potatoes are seeing heightened demand due to their perceived stability and essential nature, while discount retailers benefit from consumers tightening belts amid fears of rising prices. Pharmaceutical companies, often insulated from economic cycles, are attracting capital as investors prioritize safety over growth. The impact is profound, with market participants describing the shift as a desperate scramble for protection against unprecedented economic disruption caused by the new trade barriers.

Discount chains are benefiting immensely from consumers tightening their belts and seeking value, while drugmakers are capitalizing on heightened health concerns and consistent demand for pharmaceuticals. one_news.title: China Hits Back at US with Retaliatory Tariffs in Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: In a dramatic escalation of trade tensions, China's Ministry of Commerce announced on April 4, 2025, that it will impose a retaliatory tariff of 34% on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action is a direct response to the Trump administration's sweeping tariffs announced earlier in the week, which targeted Chinese products. A spokesperson for the ministry stated that the move was necessary to defend China's national interests against what was described as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has sent shockwaves through global financial markets, causing widespread panic and leading to sharp declines in Asian and European stock indexes, while US futures plummeted amid intensifying fears of a global recession. The causal chain of events highlights a deepening rift between the world's two largest economies, with potential long-term implications for international trade and economic stability.

The escalating trade tensions have intensified fears of a potential global recession, as the tit-for-tat measures threaten to disrupt international supply chains and economic stability worldwide.

one_news.title: China Retaliates with Sweeping Tariffs on US Goods Amid Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: In a sharp escalation of trade tensions, China's Ministry of Commerce announced today that it will impose a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action comes as a direct response to the Trump administration's recent imposition of sweeping tariffs earlier this week. A spokesperson for the ministry emphasized that this measure is essential to defend China's national interests against what they describe as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has triggered widespread panic across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing significant declines and US futures plummeting sharply. Fears of a deepening global recession are intensifying, as this tit-for-tat tariff war threatens to disrupt international trade flows and economic stability worldwide.

one_news.title: China Imposes Retaliatory Tariffs on All US Imports Amid Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: In a dramatic escalation of the ongoing trade conflict, China's Ministry of Commerce has announced the imposition of a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action comes as a direct response to the Trump administration's recent implementation of sweeping tariffs, which were unveiled earlier this week. A spokesperson for the ministry emphasized that this measure is essential to defend China's national interests against what they described as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has triggered a profound and immediate reaction across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing severe declines and US futures plummeting sharply. Investors and analysts are expressing heightened fears that this tit-for-tat tariff war could precipitate a global recession, as trade tensions between the world's two largest economies reach unprecedented levels. The move underscores the deepening rift in international trade relations and raises concerns about the stability of the global economic order.

one_news.title: China Imposes Retaliatory Tariffs on All US Goods in Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: BEIJING, April 4 (Reuters) - China's Ministry of Commerce announced on Friday that it will impose a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States, directly responding to recent measures by the Trump administration. A spokesperson for the ministry stated that this action is necessary to defend China's national interests against what it described as unilateral protectionism. The announcement has triggered widespread panic across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing significant declines and U.S. futures falling sharply. This move intensifies fears of a deepening global recession, as the trade war between the world's two largest economies escalates further.

one_news.title: China Hits Back at US with Retaliatory Tariffs in Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: In a dramatic escalation of trade tensions, China's Ministry of Commerce announced on April 4, 2025, that it will impose a retaliatory tariff of 34% on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action is a direct response to the Trump administration's sweeping tariffs announced earlier in the week, which targeted Chinese products. A spokesperson for the ministry stated that the move was necessary to defend China's national interests against what was described as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has sent shockwaves through global financial markets, causing widespread panic and leading to sharp declines in Asian and European stock indexes, while US futures plummeted amid intensifying fears of a global recession. The causal chain of events highlights a deepening rift between the world's two largest economies, with potential long-term implications for international trade and economic stability.

one_news.content: In a sharp escalation of trade tensions, China's Ministry of Commerce announced today that it will impose a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action comes as a direct response to the Trump administration's recent imposition of sweeping tariffs earlier this week. A spokesperson for the ministry emphasized that this measure is essential to defend China's national interests against what they describe as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has triggered widespread panic across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing significant declines and US futures plummeting sharply. Fears of a deepening global recession are intensifying, as this tit-for-tat tariff war threatens to disrupt international trade flows and economic stability worldwide.

one_news.title: China Imposes Retaliatory Tariffs on All US Goods, Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: China's Ministry of Commerce has announced the imposition of a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States, a direct response to the Trump administration's recent sweeping tariffs. A spokesperson for the ministry stated that this measure is necessary to defend China's national interests against unilateral protectionism. The announcement has triggered a fresh wave of panic through global financial markets, causing Asian and European stock indexes to plunge and sending U.S. futures sharply lower amid escalating fears of a global recession. This move intensifies the trade conflict, with potential severe consequences for international trade and economic stability.

one_news.title: China Imposes Retaliatory Tariffs on All US Imports Amid Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: In a dramatic escalation of the ongoing trade conflict, China's Ministry of Commerce has announced the imposition of a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action comes as a direct response to the Trump administration's recent implementation of sweeping tariffs, which were unveiled earlier this week. A spokesperson for the ministry emphasized that this measure is essential to defend China's national interests against what they described as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has triggered a profound and immediate reaction across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing severe declines and US futures plummeting sharply. Investors and analysts are expressing heightened fears that this tit-for-tat tariff war could precipitate a global recession, as trade tensions between the world's two largest economies reach unprecedented levels. The move underscores the deepening rift in international trade relations and raises concerns about the stability of the global economic order.

one_news.content: BEIJING, April 4 (Reuters) - China's Ministry of Commerce announced on Friday that it will impose a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States, directly responding to recent measures by the Trump administration. A spokesperson for the ministry stated that this action is necessary to defend China's national interests against what it described as unilateral protectionism. The announcement has triggered widespread panic across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing significant declines and U.S. futures falling sharply. This move intensifies fears of a deepening global recession, as the trade war between the world's two largest economies escalates further.

one_news.title: China Imposes Retaliatory Tariffs on All US Imports Amid Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: China's Ministry of Commerce has announced the imposition of a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States, directly responding to recent measures by the Trump administration. A spokesperson for the ministry emphasized that this action is essential to protect China's national interests against what is described as unilateral protectionism. The announcement has triggered widespread panic across global financial markets, with significant declines observed in Asian and European stock indexes and sharp drops in U.S. futures. This development intensifies fears of a deepening global recession, as the trade conflict between the world's two largest economies escalates further.

one_news.title: China Hits Back at US with Retaliatory Tariffs in Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: In a dramatic escalation of trade tensions, China's Ministry of Commerce announced on April 4, 2025, that it will impose a retaliatory tariff of 34% on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action is a direct response to the Trump administration's sweeping tariffs announced earlier in the week, which targeted Chinese products. A spokesperson for the ministry stated that the move was necessary to defend China's national interests against what was described as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has sent shockwaves through global financial markets, causing widespread panic and leading to sharp declines in Asian and European stock indexes, while US futures plummeted amid intensifying fears of a global recession. The causal chain of events highlights a deepening rift between the world's two largest economies, with potential long-term implications for international trade and economic stability.

one_news.title: China Imposes Retaliatory Tariffs on All US Imports, Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: In a decisive move, China's Ministry of Commerce has announced the imposition of a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States. This action is a direct response to the Trump administration's recent sweeping tariffs, which were unveiled earlier this week. A spokesperson for the ministry emphasized that this measure is essential to defend China's national interests against what they termed unilateral protectionism. The announcement has triggered a severe panic across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing sharp declines and U.S. futures plummeting. The escalating trade tensions have intensified fears of a potential global recession, as the tit-for-tat measures threaten to disrupt international supply chains and economic stability worldwide.

one_news.title: China Retaliates with Sweeping Tariffs on US Goods Amid Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: In a sharp escalation of trade tensions, China's Ministry of Commerce announced today that it will impose a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action comes as a direct response to the Trump administration's recent imposition of sweeping tariffs earlier this week. A spokesperson for the ministry emphasized that this measure is essential to defend China's national interests against what they describe as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has triggered widespread panic across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing significant declines and US futures plummeting sharply. Fears of a deepening global recession are intensifying, as this tit-for-tat tariff war threatens to disrupt international trade flows and economic stability worldwide.

one_news.content: In a dramatic escalation of the ongoing trade conflict, China's Ministry of Commerce has announced the imposition of a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action comes as a direct response to the Trump administration's recent implementation of sweeping tariffs, which were unveiled earlier this week. A spokesperson for the ministry emphasized that this measure is essential to defend China's national interests against what they described as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has triggered a profound and immediate reaction across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing severe declines and US futures plummeting sharply. Investors and analysts are expressing heightened fears that this tit-for-tat tariff war could precipitate a global recession, as trade tensions between the world's two largest economies reach unprecedented levels. The move underscores the deepening rift in international trade relations and raises concerns about the stability of the global economic order.

one_news.title: China Imposes Retaliatory Tariffs on All US Goods in Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: BEIJING, April 4 (Reuters) - China's Ministry of Commerce announced on Friday that it will impose a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States, directly responding to recent measures by the Trump administration. A spokesperson for the ministry stated that this action is necessary to defend China's national interests against what it described as unilateral protectionism. The announcement has triggered widespread panic across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing significant declines and U.S. futures falling sharply. This move intensifies fears of a deepening global recession, as the trade war between the world's two largest economies escalates further.

The announcement has triggered widespread panic in global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing significant declines and U.S. futures falling sharply. This escalation in trade tensions has heightened fears of a potential global recession, as the causal chain of retaliatory actions continues to unfold without resolution.

one_news.title: China Hits Back at US with Retaliatory Tariffs in Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: In a dramatic escalation of trade tensions, China's Ministry of Commerce announced on April 4, 2025, that it will impose a retaliatory tariff of 34% on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action is a direct response to the Trump administration's sweeping tariffs announced earlier in the week, which targeted Chinese products. A spokesperson for the ministry stated that the move was necessary to defend China's national interests against what was described as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has sent shockwaves through global financial markets, causing widespread panic and leading to sharp declines in Asian and European stock indexes, while US futures plummeted amid intensifying fears of a global recession. The causal chain of events highlights a deepening rift between the world's two largest economies, with potential long-term implications for international trade and economic stability.

one_news.content: In a sharp escalation of trade tensions, China's Ministry of Commerce announced today that it will impose a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action comes as a direct response to the Trump administration's recent imposition of sweeping tariffs earlier this week. A spokesperson for the ministry emphasized that this measure is essential to defend China's national interests against what they describe as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has triggered widespread panic across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing significant declines and US futures plummeting sharply. Fears of a deepening global recession are intensifying, as this tit-for-tat tariff war threatens to disrupt international trade flows and economic stability worldwide.

available_strategy: strategy_1: Update the 20-trade and 50-trade moving average lines with the mid-price of the latest 20 and 50 best ask and best bid respectively. Buy when the 20-trade moving average line crosses above the 50-trade moving average line, and sell when the 20-trade moving average line crosses below the 50-trade moving average line.
strategy_2: Give what you think is the true price of the current stock. Buy when the stock price is lower than that price and sell when it is higher than that price

strategy_3: Calculate the MACD bar using the median price between on best ask and best bid in the most recent 26 updated order books. Buy when DIFF crosses above DEA and sell when DIFF crosses below DEA

one_news.content: In a dramatic escalation of the ongoing trade conflict, China's Ministry of Commerce has announced the imposition of a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action comes as a direct response to the Trump administration's recent implementation of sweeping tariffs, which were unveiled earlier this week. A spokesperson for the ministry emphasized that this measure is essential to defend China's national interests against what they described as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has triggered a profound and immediate reaction across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing severe declines and US futures plummeting sharply. Investors and analysts are expressing heightened fears that this tit-for-tat tariff war could precipitate a global recession, as trade tensions between the world's two largest economies reach unprecedented levels. The move underscores the deepening rift in international trade relations and raises concerns about the stability of the global economic order.

one_news.title: China Imposes Retaliatory Tariffs on All US Goods in Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: BEIJING, April 4 (Reuters) - China's Ministry of Commerce announced on Friday that it will impose a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States, directly responding to recent measures by the Trump administration. A spokesperson for the ministry stated that this action is necessary to defend China's national interests against what it described as unilateral protectionism. The announcement has triggered widespread panic across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing significant declines and U.S. futures falling sharply. This move intensifies fears of a deepening global recession, as the trade war between the world's two largest economies escalates further.

one_news.title: China Hits Back at US with Retaliatory Tariffs in Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: In a dramatic escalation of trade tensions, China's Ministry of Commerce announced on April 4, 2025, that it will impose a retaliatory tariff of 34% on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action is a direct response to the Trump administration's sweeping tariffs announced earlier in the week, which targeted Chinese products. A spokesperson for the ministry stated that the move was necessary to defend China's national interests against what was described as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has sent shockwaves through global financial markets, causing widespread panic and leading to sharp declines in Asian and European stock indexes, while US futures plummeted amid intensifying fears of a global recession. The causal chain of events highlights a deepening rift between the world's two largest economies, with potential long-term implications for international trade and economic stability.

This move marks a significant escalation in the ongoing trade war, raising concerns about prolonged international tensions and their devastating impact on global trade flows.

one_news.content: In a sharp escalation of trade tensions, China's Ministry of Commerce announced today that it will impose a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action comes as a direct response to the Trump administration's recent imposition of sweeping tariffs earlier this week. A spokesperson for the ministry emphasized that this measure is essential to defend China's national interests against what they describe as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has triggered widespread panic across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing significant declines and US futures plummeting sharply. Fears of a deepening global recession are intensifying, as this tit-for-tat tariff war threatens to disrupt international trade flows and economic stability worldwide.

one_news.title: China Imposes Retaliatory Tariffs on All US Goods, Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: China's Ministry of Commerce has announced the imposition of a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States, a direct response to the Trump administration's recent sweeping tariffs. A spokesperson for the ministry stated that this measure is necessary to defend China's national interests against unilateral protectionism. The announcement has triggered a fresh wave of panic through global financial markets, causing Asian and European stock indexes to plunge and sending U.S. futures sharply lower amid escalating fears of a global recession. This move intensifies the trade conflict, with potential severe consequences for international trade and economic stability.

one_news.content: In a dramatic escalation of the ongoing trade conflict, China's Ministry of Commerce has announced the imposition of a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States. This decisive action comes as a direct response to the Trump administration's recent implementation of sweeping tariffs, which were unveiled earlier this week. A spokesperson for the ministry emphasized that this measure is essential to defend China's national interests against what they described as unilateral protectionism by the US. The announcement has triggered a profound and immediate reaction across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing severe declines and US futures plummeting sharply. Investors and analysts are expressing heightened fears that this tit-for-tat tariff war could precipitate a global recession, as trade tensions between the world's two largest economies reach unprecedented levels. The move underscores the deepening rift in international trade relations and raises concerns about the stability of the global economic order.

one_news.title: China Imposes Retaliatory Tariffs on All US Goods in Escalating Trade War
one_news.content: BEIJING, April 4 (Reuters) - China's Ministry of Commerce announced on Friday that it will impose a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States, directly responding to recent measures by the Trump administration. A spokesperson for the ministry stated that this action is necessary to defend China's national interests against what it described as unilateral protectionism. The announcement has triggered widespread panic across global financial markets, with Asian and European stock indexes experiencing significant declines and U.S. futures falling sharply. This move intensifies fears of a deepening global recession, as the trade war between the world's two largest economies escalates further.

one_news.content: China's Ministry of Commerce has announced the imposition of a retaliatory tariff on all imported goods originating from the United States, directly responding to recent measures by the Trump administration. A spokesperson for the ministry emphasized that this action is essential to protect China's national interests against what is described as unilateral protectionism. The announcement has triggered widespread panic across global financial markets, with significant declines observed in Asian and European stock indexes and sharp drops in U.S. futures. This development intensifies fears of a deepening global recession, as the trade conflict between the world's two largest economies escalates further.

one_news.title: Johnson & Johnson's Tremfya Achieves Breakthrough in Psoriatic Arthritis Study, Transforming Treatment Landscape
one_news.content: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) announced today that its drug Tremfya (guselkumab) has demonstrated unprecedented efficacy in a late-stage study for psoriatic arthritis, marking a monumental shift in patient care. The Phase 3b APEX study, involving biologic-naïve patients with inadequate response to standard therapies, successfully met its primary endpoint of ACR20a, significantly reducing disease signs and symptoms, and achieved its major secondary endpoint by halting structural damage progression as measured radiographically at 24 weeks compared to placebo. This outcome is set to revolutionize treatment protocols, offering new hope for countless individuals suffering from this debilitating condition. The findings underscore Tremfya's potential to become a cornerstone therapy, with implications that could reshape the entire pharmaceutical approach to autoimmune diseases. Experts are hailing this as a watershed moment, predicting widespread adoption and profound improvements in patient quality of life globally.

one_news.title: Johnson & Johnson's Tremfya Achieves Breakthrough in Psoriatic Arthritis Study
one_news.content: NEW YORK, April 4 (Reuters) - Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) announced on Friday that its drug Tremfya (guselkumab) has demonstrated significant efficacy in a late-stage study for psoriatic arthritis, marking a pivotal advancement in treatment options. The Phase 3b APEX study, involving biologic-naïve patients with inadequate response to standard therapies, successfully met its primary endpoint of reducing signs and symptoms, as measured by ACR20, and its major secondary endpoint of reducing structural damage progression at 24 weeks compared to placebo. This outcome could revolutionize the management of psoriatic arthritis, potentially offering new hope for millions of patients worldwide and solidifying Johnson & Johnson's leadership in immunology. The results are expected to have an immense impact on the pharmaceutical landscape, driving unprecedented shifts in treatment protocols and patient care standards.

one_news.title: Johnson & Johnson's Tremfya Shows Efficacy In Late-Stage Psoriatic Arthritis Study
one_news.content: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) announced topline results from its Phase 3b APEX study of Tremfya (guselkumab) in patients with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA) who are biologic naïve and have had an inadequate response to standard therapies. The study achieved its primary endpoint of reducing signs and symptoms and its major secondary endpoint of reducing progression of structural damage as measured by radiographic progression at 24 weeks compared to placebo. This breakthrough could revolutionize treatment options for millions of patients worldwide, potentially leading to unprecedented improvements in quality of life and setting a new standard in biologic therapies for autoimmune diseases. The findings are expected to have a profound and immediate impact on the pharmaceutical industry, driving significant interest and investment in similar treatments.

one_news.title: Johnson & Johnson's Tremfya Achieves Breakthrough in Psoriatic Arthritis Study, Potentially Transforming Treatment Landscape
one_news.content: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) has announced groundbreaking topline results from its Phase 3b APEX study of Tremfya (guselkumab) in patients with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA) who are biologic naïve and have had an inadequate response to standard therapies. The study successfully met its primary endpoint of ACR20a, significantly reducing signs and symptoms, and its major secondary endpoint of reducing progression of structural damage as measured by radiographic progression at 24 weeks compared to placebo. This development could lead to a paradigm shift in the management of psoriatic arthritis, offering new hope for patients worldwide. The findings are expected to have a profound impact on the pharmaceutical industry and healthcare systems, potentially setting a new standard for treatment efficacy and patient outcomes.

one_news.title: Johnson & Johnson's Tremfya Achieves Breakthrough in Psoriatic Arthritis Study, Potentially Transforming Treatment Landscape
one_news.content: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) announced today that its drug Tremfya (guselkumab) has demonstrated unprecedented efficacy in a late-stage study for psoriatic arthritis (PsA), marking a monumental advancement in medical science. The Phase 3b APEX study, involving biologic-naïve patients with inadequate response to standard therapies, successfully met its primary endpoint of ACR20a, significantly reducing disease signs and symptoms, and achieved its major secondary endpoint by halting structural damage progression as measured radiographically at 24 weeks compared to placebo. This outcome is poised to revolutionize treatment protocols globally, offering new hope for millions suffering from this debilitating condition. The findings underscore Tremfya's potential to become a cornerstone therapy, with implications that could reshape the entire pharmaceutical industry and patient care standards.

one_news.title: Johnson & Johnson's Tremfya Achieves Key Endpoints in Psoriatic Arthritis Study, Potentially Transforming Treatment Landscape
one_news.content: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) announced on Friday that its drug Tremfya (guselkumab) has demonstrated significant efficacy in a late-stage study for psoriatic arthritis, marking a potential breakthrough in treatment options for patients. The Phase 3b APEX study, which focused on biologic-naïve patients with active psoriatic arthritis who had inadequate responses to standard therapies, successfully met its primary endpoint of ACR20, indicating a substantial reduction in disease signs and symptoms. Additionally, the study achieved its major secondary endpoint by showing a notable reduction in radiographic progression of structural damage at 24 weeks compared to placebo. This development could have profound implications for the healthcare sector, potentially leading to widespread adoption and significant improvements in patient outcomes, while also influencing pharmaceutical research and development strategies globally. The findings underscore the importance of innovative biologic treatments in addressing complex autoimmune conditions, and may prompt regulatory reviews and expanded usage in clinical practice.

one_news.title: Johnson & Johnson's Tremfya Achieves Breakthrough in Late-Stage Psoriatic Arthritis Study
one_news.content: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) announced on Friday that its drug Tremfya (guselkumab) has demonstrated significant efficacy in a Phase 3b APEX study for patients with active psoriatic arthritis who are biologic naïve and have had an inadequate response to standard therapies. The study successfully met its primary endpoint of reducing signs and symptoms, as well as its major secondary endpoint of reducing progression of structural damage, compared to placebo at 24 weeks. This development is poised to revolutionize treatment options for psoriatic arthritis, potentially offering new hope for millions of patients worldwide. The findings could lead to a dramatic shift in the pharmaceutical landscape, with Tremfya becoming a cornerstone therapy in this challenging disease area.

one_news.title: Johnson & Johnson's Tremfya Achieves Key Endpoints in Psoriatic Arthritis Study, Potentially Transforming Treatment Landscape
one_news.content: Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) announced on Friday that its drug Tremfya (guselkumab) has demonstrated significant efficacy in a Phase 3b APEX study for patients with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA) who are biologic naïve and have had an inadequate response to standard therapies. The study successfully met its primary endpoint of ACR20, which measures a reduction in signs and symptoms, and its major secondary endpoint of reducing progression of structural damage as assessed by radiographic progression at 24 weeks compared to placebo. This breakthrough could lead to a paradigm shift in the management of psoriatic arthritis, offering new hope for patients who have struggled with limited treatment options. The findings from the APEX study underscore the potential for Tremfya to become a cornerstone therapy, with implications that could extend to broader autoimmune conditions, fundamentally altering the standard of care and providing immense relief to millions affected worldwide.
